readerQuestion: How are SNAP benefits calculated? [PAA 0/0; ac 9/9 on-topic, 4/9 calculation-method]
decisionGap: The strongest lookup matches are /compare/1099-vs-w2/ (pay/tax compensation) and /guides/ssi-and-inheritance/ (inheritance and SSI), neither computes food allotments. Same-run application guide answers submitting an application, and WIC comparison answers program differences. No exact route history at local HEAD or pinned published850b1e4; final /budget/ route lookup separately saved.
finding: Calculated, with explicit hypothetical inputs: for four people and $2,000 earned monthly income, $1,200 allowed shelter, no other deductions, standard deduction $229 gives net $856.50 and conditional full-month benefit $766. Raising allowed shelter to $1,400 gives $826 before shelter cap binds. Use current COLA constants and our own arithmetic, not USDA’s internally inconsistent worked example. Visible wording will identify our calculation and link a nearby method/inputs table.
conditions: Client-side deterministic React island. Inputs: household1–8, monthly earned/unearned income, necessary dependent care, state-allowed child support, elderly/disabled flag and medical costs, rent/mortgage plus state-approved utility allowance. Standard deductions [217,217,217,229,268,308,308,308]; 20% earned deduction; medical excess above$35 where eligible; excess shelter above half adjusted income, cap$769 unless elderly/disabled. Max allotments [306,562,808,1023,1217,1463,1616,1841]; subtract ceil(0.3×net). Show raw formula and conditional eligible1–2-member $25 minimum distinctly; suppress an award-like amount above federal net reference unless the user explicitly confirms a state eligibility determination. No estimate for AK/HI/territories or9+; link official tables. Defaults are a disclosed hypothetical four-person case. Copy/download result and inputs; no server submission. Validate all boundaries, mobile390px and keyboard access.
whatWouldChange: Net income and allowed deductions determine a conditional amount up to the household maximum. Use the breakdown and current state allowances to plan, then have the state decide eligibility. Different deductions, state options, first-month dates or a revised COLA change the answer.
